question: Can the 1959 number 3368 and corrected 1987 number 3288 be semantically classified from each catalog's own rules, and can the 1987 compilation context narrow the possible cause of the object-specific number change without inventing a renumbering rule?
answer: Yes at the catalog-semantics and compilation-context level. Direct no-OCR review of the 1959 编例 states that numbers below titles are 书号, so target 3368 is a historical book number, not merely an unexplained printed sequence. Direct no-OCR review of the 1987 前言/编例 shows that the new catalog was compiled afresh beginning in 1986, covered holdings acquired from 1910 through 1986, and explicitly says it corrected some earlier cataloging errors; its 编例 likewise defines the number below each title as 书号. Combined with Batch 12HS's corrected target 3288 and unchanged neighboring control 10010 across the two catalogs, this closes a recompilation/correction environment and disproves a blanket arithmetic renumbering. It does not identify the exact target-specific event that changed 3368 to 3288.
